title: The Essentials — Wii's Signature Library
blurb: The system-sellers. Every one of these helped turn the Wii into the best-selling console of its generation, and most still headline any conversation about the platform's best games.

games.title: Wii Sports
games.blurb: The pack-in game that put a motion controller in tens of millions of living rooms and briefly made bowling a family sport again.

games.title: Wii Sports Resort
games.blurb: MotionPlus-powered precision turned a simple sequel into one of the clearest showcases of what Wii motion control could actually do.

games.title: Wii Play
games.blurb: Nine simple minigames bundled with a second Remote, quietly one of the best-selling games in history almost by accident.

games.title: Mario Kart Wii
games.blurb: Bikes, a steering-wheel peripheral, and online racing made this the best-selling entry in the entire Mario Kart series.

games.title: Super Mario Galaxy
games.blurb: Gravity-bending planetoid platforming that's still regularly named among the best 3D platformers ever made.

games.title: Super Mario Galaxy 2
games.blurb: A denser, more inventive sequel that many fans and critics consider an improvement on an already-perfect original.

games.title: Super Smash Bros. Brawl
games.blurb: Adds a story mode, Subspace Emissary, and a much bigger roster to Nintendo's crossover fighter, played competitively for years after release.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess
games.blurb: A darker, more mature Zelda launched alongside the console itself, with motion-controlled swordplay built right into the pack-in launch window.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
games.blurb: MotionPlus-driven one-to-one sword combat and a sky-island structure that closes out the Wii's Zelda output on an ambitious note.

games.title: Metroid Prime 3: Corruption
games.blurb: Pointer-based aiming brought Samus's first-person adventures to Wii with some of the series' most precise, responsive controls yet.

games.title: Metroid Prime Trilogy
games.blurb: All three Prime games rebuilt with Wii controls in one collection, widely considered the definitive way to play the series.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country Returns
games.blurb: A brutally difficult, gorgeously animated revival of the SNES series from the studio that had just finished reinventing Metroid.

games.title: New Super Mario Bros. Wii
games.blurb: Four-player simultaneous co-op turned 2D Mario into a chaotic, screen-clearing party game overnight.

games.title: Wii Fit
games.blurb: The Balance Board peripheral and daily weigh-ins turned exercise gaming into a genuine cultural phenomenon.

title: Motion-Control Action & Third-Party Standouts
blurb: The games that took the Wii Remote seriously as a combat tool — waggle-powered swordplay, katana-slicing, and a boxing revival that used motion control better than almost anything else on the system.

games.title: Resident Evil 4: Wii Edition
games.blurb: The GameCube classic remapped around Wii Remote aiming, with many longtime fans calling this the best way to play it.

games.title: No More Heroes
games.blurb: Suda51's beam-katana assassin comedy turned Wii Remote slashing into a stylish, self-aware send-up of open-world game design.

games.title: No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle
games.blurb: A faster, funnier sequel that trims the original's open-world padding in favor of pure boss-rush momentum.

games.title: MadWorld
games.blurb: Black-and-white, blood-red ultraviolence rendered in a comic-book art style, with motion-controlled executions built for maximum spectacle.

games.title: Red Steel 2
games.blurb: MotionPlus sword combat and gunplay in a spaghetti-western-meets-samurai setting, widely regarded as proof the tech could finally deliver.

games.title: Punch-Out!!
games.blurb: A loving revival of the NES boxing classic with motion-controlled jabs, dodges, and uppercuts that never feel like a gimmick.

games.title: Zack & Wiki: Quest for Barbaros' Treasure
games.blurb: A pointer-driven puzzle-adventure about turning cursed pirates' enemies into tools, endearing and cruelly clever in equal measure.

games.title: Sin and Punishment: Star Successor
games.blurb: A blistering on-rails shooter from cult favorite developer Treasure, praised for some of the tightest bullet-dodging action on the system.

games.title: Tatsunoko vs. Capcom: Ultimate All-Stars
games.blurb: A crossover fighter pairing Capcom characters with classic Tatsunoko anime heroes most Western players had never heard of before.

games.title: Okami
games.blurb: The PS2 original's sumi-e brush mechanics translated naturally onto Wii's pointer controls, giving the celestial-brush adventure a fitting second home.

title: JRPGs & Long Adventures
blurb: A smaller shelf than other consoles, but a fiercely beloved one — Operation Rainfall's fan campaign to localize this chapter's first three games became gaming folklore in its own right.

games.title: Xenoblade Chronicles
games.blurb: A sprawling open-world JRPG fought on the backs of two frozen titans, released in Europe in August 2011 — Nintendo of America held off for another eight months, reaching North America only in April 2012 after the fan-driven Operation Rainfall campaign forced its hand.

games.title: The Last Story
games.blurb: Hironobu Sakaguchi's real-time tactical RPG reached Europe in February 2012, months ahead of a North American release that didn't arrive until that August — one of the three Operation Rainfall imports fans had to campaign to see localized.

games.title: Pandora's Tower
games.blurb: A dark, romance-driven action-RPG about feeding monster flesh to a cursed heroine, published by Nintendo in Europe in April 2012 — North America didn't get it at all until Xseed stepped in a full year later.

games.title: Fragile Dreams: Farewell Ruins of the Moon
games.blurb: A quiet, melancholy adventure through a post-apocalyptic Japan where loneliness is as much the antagonist as anything else.

games.title: Monster Hunter Tri
games.blurb: Underwater combat and a fresh set of monsters gave the series a proper Western console debut, complete with a Classic Controller Pro bundle.

games.title: Tales of Symphonia: Dawn of the New World
games.blurb: A direct sequel to the GameCube original, following a new protagonist through the world Lloyd and company left behind.

games.title: Arc Rise Fantasia
games.blurb: A traditional turn-based JRPG with an idol-pop theme song and a small but devoted following among Wii RPG fans.

games.title: Baroque
games.blurb: A surreal, punishing roguelike remake of a Saturn-era cult classic, as disorienting narratively as it is mechanically.

title: Platformers
blurb: From Nintendo's own yarn-textured reinvention of Kirby to a hand-painted samurai epic and a PC indie darling making its console debut, Wii's platforming shelf ran wonderfully wide.

games.title: Kirby's Epic Yarn
games.blurb: Kirby loses his signature copy ability but gains an entire world made of fabric, yarn, and buttons — one of the most purely charming games on the system.

games.title: Kirby's Return to Dream Land
games.blurb: A return to classic Kirby platforming with copy abilities restored and four-player co-op layered on top — released the same year in Europe under a different title, Kirby's Adventure Wii.

games.title: Super Paper Mario
games.blurb: A dimension-flipping hybrid of platforming and RPG systems that swapped turn-based battles for real-time jumping and dashing.

games.title: Rayman Origins
games.blurb: Gorgeous hand-drawn animation and tight platforming marked a full-scale revival for a series that had drifted from its roots.

games.title: Muramasa: The Demon Blade
games.blurb: Hand-painted 2D samurai action across two interwoven stories, one of the most visually striking games the Wii ever received.

games.title: A Boy and His Blob
games.blurb: A reimagining of the NES classic where feeding a shapeshifting blob different jellybeans solves the game's puzzles.

games.title: LostWinds
games.blurb: A wind-manipulation platformer controlled entirely with the Wii Remote pointer, one of WiiWare's earliest and best original games.

games.title: de Blob
games.blurb: Roll a paint-absorbing blob through a monochrome city to restore its color, a colorful, upbeat spin on collect-a-thon platforming.

games.title: Klonoa
games.blurb: A remake of the beloved PS1 platformer with redrawn visuals, reintroducing the series' dream-world charm to a new generation.

games.title: Cave Story
games.blurb: The beloved PC indie classic's console debut, bringing its Metroidvania exploration and surprisingly deep story to Wii for the first time.

title: Rhythm, Music & Party
blurb: Plastic instruments took over living rooms this generation, and Wii got its own versions of almost all of them, alongside Nintendo's own thoroughly weird music and minigame experiments.

games.title: Rhythm Heaven Fever
games.blurb: A collection of bizarre, deceptively simple rhythm minigames that built a small but fiercely devoted cult following.

games.title: Rock Band 2
games.blurb: The band-simulation phenomenon's Wii port, bringing four-instrument co-op rock stardom to the console a year after launch.

games.title: Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock
games.blurb: The Wii port of the series' commercial peak, with wireless guitar peripherals and a setlist stacked with genuine rock classics.

games.title: Guitar Hero: World Tour
games.blurb: Adds drums and vocals to the guitar formula, turning the series into a full-band experience on Wii.

games.title: DJ Hero
games.blurb: A turntable peripheral and scratch-based rhythm mechanics gave the genre a genuinely fresh spin after years of guitar-shaped clones.

games.title: WarioWare: Smooth Moves
games.blurb: Hundreds of five-second microgames built entirely around goofy Wii Remote poses, one of the purest expressions of the console's whole philosophy.

games.title: Wii Music
games.blurb: A famously divisive experiment in gesture-based musical performance rather than rhythm-accuracy scoring, more toy than game by design.

games.title: Mario Party 8
games.blurb: Motion-controlled minigames layered onto the classic board-game formula — the UK release was pulled from shelves and quietly patched within weeks of launch after one minigame's script used a word that reads as a slur in British English but not American.

games.title: Wii Party
games.blurb: A minigame collection built specifically around the Wii Remote and Balance Board rather than retrofitting an existing Mario Party formula.

title: On-Rails & Light-Gun Shooters
blurb: The Wii Remote's pointer made it the best home light-gun controller ever built, and this genre enjoyed a small renaissance here that it hasn't really had since.

games.title: Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles
games.blurb: Retells the events of the first three Resident Evil games as an on-rails shooter, built specifically around Wii pointer aiming.

games.title: Resident Evil: The Darkside Chronicles
games.blurb: A follow-up covering Resident Evil 2 and Code: Veronica, with reworked pacing that leans harder into cinematic set pieces.

games.title: The House of the Dead: Overkill
games.blurb: A gleefully trashy grindhouse throwback packed with profanity and gore, one of the most purely fun light-gun games on the system.

games.title: The House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return
games.blurb: A double-pack remaster of two arcade classics, rebuilt around Wii Zapper aiming for the home light-gun crowd.

games.title: Ghost Squad
games.blurb: An arcade counter-terrorism shooter ported to Wii with Zapper support, prized for its multiple branching mission routes.

games.title: Dead Space: Extraction
games.blurb: A prequel telling the story behind the original Dead Space through on-rails horror-shooter sequences, better regarded than its sales suggested.

games.title: Link's Crossbow Training
games.blurb: A Zelda-themed light-gun game bundled with the Wii Zapper peripheral, built to show off pointer precision more than tell a story.

title: Horror & Mystery
blurb: From a reimagined psychological Silent Hill built specifically for Wii to two courtroom dramas that found an unlikely home here, this chapter shows a quieter, stranger side of the console.

games.title: Silent Hill: Shattered Memories
games.blurb: A ground-up reimagining rather than a remake, restructuring the original game's story around psychological profiling that changes the game as you play.

games.title: Cursed Mountain
games.blurb: A Himalayan mountaineering horror game blending real-world survival tension with vengeful-spirit combat, an overlooked genre entry from an Austrian studio.

games.title: Fatal Frame: Mask of the Lunar Eclipse
games.blurb: A camera-as-weapon horror game co-developed with Suda51's studio, released only in Japan on Wii and long sought after by import collectors.

games.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
games.blurb: The courtroom-drama visual novel's WiiWare debut, bringing its objection-shouting mystery-solving to a new control scheme.

games.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney: Trials and Tribulations
games.blurb: The third mainline Ace Attorney case, arriving on WiiWare with its emotionally heavier storyline intact.

games.title: Trauma Center: New Blood
games.blurb: Motion-controlled surgery under time pressure, with two playable surgeons and co-op operations layered onto the series' tense formula.

games.title: Trauma Team
games.blurb: Expands the surgery formula into six different medical specialties, each with its own distinct motion-control mechanics.

title: Racing & Sports
blurb: Beyond Mario Kart Wii already up top, the console's racing and sports shelf leaned hard into arcade spectacle — off-road demolition derbies, robot-animal races, and snowboarding gone genuinely strange.

games.title: Excite Truck
games.blurb: Launch-window off-road racing with wildly deformable terrain, built to show off what tilt-and-motion steering could feel like.

games.title: ExciteBots: Trick Racing
games.blurb: A stranger, funnier sequel starring robot-animal racers, beloved by the small audience that actually found it.

games.title: Mario Strikers Charged
games.blurb: Arcade soccer with no rules, illegal tackles, and Mega Strikes capable of wiping out a goalkeeper entirely.

games.title: Mario Power Tennis (New Play Control!)
games.blurb: A Wii-controlled re-release of the GameCube tennis game, with swing-based motion controls replacing button timing.

games.title: Deca Sports
games.blurb: Ten arcade sports crammed into one motion-controlled package, a launch-era party-sports favorite despite its scattershot ambitions.

games.title: We Ski
games.blurb: Balance Board-controlled skiing and snowboarding down a mountain that also doubled as social hangout space for up to four players.

games.title: SSX Blur
games.blurb: A Wii-exclusive entry in EA's snowboarding series, trading some of the series' speed for motion-controlled trick execution.

title: Fitness & Simulation
blurb: The Balance Board and pointer controls turned out to be a natural fit for slower, gentler genres — deep-sea diving, home cooking, and full workout routines that outsold plenty of actual games.

games.title: Wii Fit Plus
games.blurb: An expanded follow-up to Wii Fit adding custom workout routines and new Balance Board minigames.

games.title: EA Sports Active
games.blurb: A structured 30-day workout program using the Wii Remote and Nunchuk as resistance-training feedback, competing directly with Wii Fit.

games.title: Endless Ocean
games.blurb: A calm, violence-free diving sim about exploring the ocean, photographing sea life, and rescuing the occasional shipwreck survivor.

games.title: Endless Ocean: Blue World
games.blurb: A larger sequel adding a proper story and deeper sea creatures to explore, still built around the original's unhurried pace.

games.title: Cooking Mama: World Kitchen
games.blurb: A motion-controlled cooking series entry that turns chopping, stirring, and plating into minigames, disarmingly popular with non-gamers.

title: Puzzle & Strategy
blurb: A smaller shelf than most genres here, but a sharp one — a tactical RPG many still call the series' best, and two very different games about knocking blocks over.

games.title: Fire Emblem: Radiant Dawn
games.blurb: A sprawling, difficult tactical RPG spanning multiple armies and perspectives, still cited by longtime fans as a series high point.

games.title: Boom Blox
games.blurb: A Steven Spielberg-conceived physics-puzzle game about knocking down block towers, deceptively deep beneath its toy-box presentation.

games.title: Boom Blox Bash Party
games.blurb: A bigger sequel adding new block types and party modes, refining the original's throw-and-topple physics puzzles.

games.title: World of Goo
games.blurb: An indie physics-puzzle darling about building precarious structures out of living, gooey balls, one of WiiWare's clear high points.

games.title: Elebits
games.blurb: A launch-window puzzle-action game about vacuuming up tiny creatures hidden throughout increasingly chaotic, physics-driven rooms.

title: Cult Classics, Curios & Japan-Only Gems
blurb: This is where a 'best of' list earns the word explorer. A Norse mecha-battler, a farming-RPG hybrid, a mosquito-simulator's spiritual cousin in the form of a giant spider — the games that make the Wii library genuinely bottomless.

games.title: Little King's Story
games.blurb: A whimsical kingdom-building game with a surprisingly dark satirical streak underneath its storybook presentation.

games.title: Zangeki no Reginleiv
games.blurb: A brutal, blood-soaked Norse mythology action game where giants are torn apart limb by limb — one of the darkest things Nintendo ever published, and Japan-only.

games.title: Earth Seeker
games.blurb: A monster-hunting action-RPG with striking hand-drawn art that never made it past Japan on Wii.

games.title: Disaster: Day of Crisis
games.blurb: A disaster-survival action game bouncing between earthquakes, volcanoes, and hostage rescues, released only in Japan and Europe — never in North America.

games.title: Ju-on: The Grudge
games.blurb: A first-person horror game built around the cursed-house film series, using the Wii Remote as an in-game flashlight and phone.

games.title: Manhunt 2
games.blurb: A stealth-horror game about escaping an asylum by brutal means — the BBFC refused it a UK classification outright, and it took a court appeal and a re-edited build before it could legally reach British shelves in October 2008, a full year after its North American release.

games.title: Deadly Creatures
games.blurb: An unusual action-adventure told from the perspective of a tarantula and a scorpion, tensely atmospheric and unlike anything else on the system.

games.title: Wario Land: Shake It!
games.blurb: A hand-drawn 2D platformer bringing Wario back to his side-scrolling roots with motion-controlled shaking attacks.

games.title: Ready 2 Rumble Revolution
games.blurb: A motion-controlled revival of the cartoonish boxing series, punchy and silly in equal measure.

games.title: Rune Factory Frontier
games.blurb: A farming-sim and action-RPG hybrid where tending crops and dungeon-diving carry equal weight.

games.title: The Conduit
games.blurb: A Wii-exclusive FPS built to prove the console could handle serious shooter ambitions, with some of the sharpest aiming controls on the system.

games.title: Ivy the Kiwi?
games.blurb: A gentle, minimalist platformer from Sonic co-creator Yuji Naka about guiding a flightless bird using stretchy vines.

games.title: Kororinpa: Marble Mania
games.blurb: A tilt-controlled marble-maze game that turned the Wii Remote into a genuinely precise physical controller.

games.title: Sengoku Basara: Samurai Heroes
games.blurb: A hyper-stylized musou brawler reimagining Japan's Warring States period as a cast of anime warlords.

title: Licensed Games Done Right
blurb: Closing the collection with the genre most players write off entirely — proof that a licensed spy, superhero, or Star Wars game could still hold its own on this console.

games.title: LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga
games.blurb: The template for every LEGO game that followed, rebuilding all six Star Wars films as slapstick brick-based co-op.

games.title: LEGO Batman: The Videogame
games.blurb: Applies the LEGO formula to Gotham City, splitting missions between heroes and the villains' own playable side of the story.

games.title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed
games.blurb: A scaled-down but still spectacle-driven take on Starkiller's story, with a distinct Wii-specific build tuned around motion-controlled Force powers.

games.title: GoldenEye 007
games.blurb: A ground-up reimagining rather than a straight remake of the N64 classic, with modernized stealth mechanics and Wii pointer aiming that won over longtime fans.
